title: How to build the world's fastest voice bot: Kwindla Hultman Kramer
talk_summary: A Daily.co engineer explains how to build low-latency voice bots, emphasizing that voice-to-voice latency (~500ms target) is dominated by network hops and model time-to-first-token, and that collocating STT, LLM, and TTS in one container is the biggest lever. He also presents Pipecat, an open-source orchestration framework for real-time multimodal pipelines.

takeaways.technique: Collocate pipeline stages in one container
takeaways.what_they_do: They run STT, turn-detection, LLM inference, and TTS together in a single compute container instead of calling hosted services, to eliminate network round-trips between stages.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the most powerful tool we have today for making everything run fast in this domain is actually putting as much together into one compute container as we possibly can
takeaways.numbers: ~500-700ms voice-to-voice achievable when collocated; Gemini Pro TTFT ~900ms alone

takeaways.technique: Measure per-stage latency, not just end-to-end
takeaways.what_they_do: They instrument each pipeline stage (encode, network, STT, LLM TTFT, TTS) and stream per-stage metrics to the client so variation can be correlated with the end-to-end number.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the numbers on the edge are metrics that are being sent from the server that's doing all that work sort of on the individual pieces
takeaways.numbers: Laptop mic alone adds 30-40ms; transcription ~200ms; LLM TTFT ~100ms target

takeaways.technique: Pick models on latency-vs-quality tradeoff, not just cost
takeaways.what_they_do: They chose Deepgram for STT/TTS and Llama 3 8B over 70B because 70B couldn't hit their latency target, explicitly trading model quality for speed.
takeaways.evidence_quote: that's llama 38b I think because I could couldn't quite get 70b to run as fast as I wanted it to

takeaways.technique: Vendor-neutral pipeline framework with pluggable services
takeaways.what_they_do: Pipecat abstracts each stage (STT, LLM, TTS, vision) as a swappable service plugin so pipelines can be recomposed without rewriting orchestration.

takeaways.technique: Test the pipeline with adversarial/noisy input, not polished prompts
takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately ran the demo without prompt engineering to stress-test latency and expose failure modes (e.g. bot mishearing 'Stockholm') rather than hide them.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the idea there was not to do prompt engineering cuz clearly I could have better done a better job
